h.strategy: Borrow interaction patterns from other empirical sciences: epistasis in genetics (the effect of one mutation depends on genetic background, and beneficial mutations help fitter backgrounds less), diminishing returns in economics, and redundancy in engineered systems. Translate each pattern into a concrete conditional hypothesis about how an edit's effect varies with the parent configuration. Favor predictions that a practitioner thinking only mechanistically would get wrong, especially background-dependent sign changes and weaker gains in already-strong parents. Use conditions that many parents satisfy. In the flaw step, discard analogies that do not transfer and keep only those with a plausible general reason to hold.

hyps.why: Without the 0->3 edge, removing edge 5 leaves at most edge 4 feeding the output and can collapse the cell, whereas an existing 0->3 path buffers the loss.
A direct identity path from input to output eases optimization of the deeper 0->1->2->3 conv chain, so deepening pays off more.
With edge 0 removed node 1 carries no signal, so swapping edge 4 to pooling has near-zero effect instead of its usual penalty.
With node 1 carrying no signal, a conv on edge 4 cannot contribute, masking its usual positive effect.
If edge 5 is none, node 2 never reaches the output, so improving its input edge is masked.
Node 2 is a dead end when edge 5 is none, nullifying the benefit of a conv on edge 2.
Adding a missing residual path gives a large gain, whereas replacing an existing conv or pool on edge 3 merely trades one working op for another.
Replacing a 1x1 conv only adds spatial receptive field, a smaller gain than replacing none or pool with a full conv.
Destroying the critical input-to-output identity path costs more than replacing none (a gain) or a conv with pooling.
Replacing none on edge 0 revives node 1 and both downstream paths (edges 2 and 4), a larger gain than upgrading an existing op.
